"""Charts and listening examples for a trained HandlingNet.

    uv run python -m kipml.report [--checkpoint ...] [--run ml/runs/<latest>] [--n 150]

Writes to ml/reports/handling-poc/:
  training.png               loss curves from the training run
  suppression.png            quality gain and how much each method removes, model vs spectral gate
  mixture_waveforms.png      a held-out mixture with ground truth: waveforms and detection
  mixture_spectrograms.png   the same mixture as spectrograms: input, model, gate, true background
  real_<take>.png            our held-out real takes: before, after, what was removed
  audio/*.wav                before and after files to listen to
  REPORT.md                  the numbers and the charts
Colours follow the dataviz reference palette (validated): blue = model, orange = spectral gate,
aqua = true background (always text-labelled), grey = input.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
import numpy as np
import torch

from .audio import AUDIO, HOP, ML_ROOT, RATE, frame_db, read_wav, write_wav
from .data import Clip, _crop, load_sources, make_example
from .evaluate import load_model, si_sdr, spectral_gate
from .infer import segments
from .model import enhance, stft

SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e6e5e1"
MODEL, GATE, TRUTH, INPUT = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#8a8984"
SEQ = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("blue_seq", [SURFACE, "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"])
OUT = ML_ROOT / "reports" / "handling-poc"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "text.color": INK, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
    "axes.titlesize": 10.5, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "axes.titlelocation": "left", "font.size": 9, "legend.frameon": False,
})


def _envelope(ax, x, color, label=None):
    """Min/max envelope per 10 ms: readable at any length, unlike plotting every sample."""
    n = len(x) // HOP
    seg = x[: n * HOP].reshape(n, HOP)
    t = np.arange(n) * HOP / RATE
    ax.fill_between(t, seg.min(1), seg.max(1), color=color, linewidth=0, label=label)
    ax.set_xlim(0, len(x) / RATE)


def _spec_db(x):
    mag = stft(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(x))[None]).abs()[0].numpy().T
    return 20 * np.log10(mag + 1e-6)


def _spectrogram(ax, x, title, vmax):
    ax.imshow(_spec_db(x), origin="lower", aspect="auto", cmap=SEQ, vmin=vmax - 70, vmax=vmax,
              extent=[0, len(x) / RATE, 0, RATE / 2000])
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_ylabel("kHz"); ax.grid(False)


def training_chart(run_dir: Path):
    hist = json.load(open(run_dir / "metrics.json"))["history"]
    steps = [h["step"] for h in hist]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax = axes[0]
    for key, color, name in (("train", MODEL, "train"), ("val", GATE, "held-out")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=color, linewidth=1.8, label=name)
        ax.annotate(name, (steps[-1], hist[-1][key]), xytext=(4, 0), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, va="center")
    ax.set_title("Total loss"); ax.set_xlabel("training step"); ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    for ax, key, title in ((axes[1], "val_spec", "Suppression loss (held-out)"), (axes[2], "val_frame_bce", "Detection loss (held-out)")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=MODEL, linewidth=1.8)
        ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xlabel("training step")
    for ax in axes:
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    fig.suptitle("HandlingNet training: loss falls on mixtures it never trained on", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "training.png", dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def suppression_stats(model, src, n):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    imp = {"model": [], "gate": []}
    red = {("model", "handling"): [], ("model", "background"): [], ("gate", "handling"): [], ("gate", "background"): []}
    tp = fp = fn = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        mix, clean, labels, has = make_example(rng, src, "test", 4.0)
        out, prob = enhance(model, mix)
        gate = spectral_gate(mix)
        f_in = frame_db(mix)
        lab = labels.astype(bool) if has else np.zeros(len(f_in), bool)
        for name, y in (("model", out), ("gate", gate)):
            drop = f_in - frame_db(y)
            if lab.any():
                red[(name, "handling")].append(float(np.mean(drop[lab])))
            if (~lab).any():
                red[(name, "background")].append(float(np.mean(drop[~lab])))
        if has:
            base = si_sdr(mix, clean)
            imp["model"].append(si_sdr(out, clean) - base)
            imp["gate"].append(si_sdr(gate, clean) - base)
            pred = prob[: len(lab)] > 0.5
            tp += int((pred & lab).sum()); fp += int((pred & ~lab).sum()); fn += int((~pred & lab).sum())
    prec, rec = tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
    return {"si_sdr_improvement_db": {k: round(float(np.median(v)), 2) for k, v in imp.items()},
            "energy_removed_db": {f"{m}_{k}": round(float(np.mean(v)), 2) for (m, k), v in red.items()},
            "detection": {"precision": round(prec, 3), "recall": round(rec, 3), "f1": round(2 * prec * rec / max(prec + rec, 1e-9), 3)},
            "mixtures": n}


def suppression_chart(stats):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.6), constrained_layout=True)
    ax = axes[0]
    vals = [stats["si_sdr_improvement_db"]["model"], stats["si_sdr_improvement_db"]["gate"]]
    bars = ax.bar(["Kip model", "Spectral gate"], vals, color=[MODEL, GATE], width=0.5, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=2)
    for b, v in zip(bars, vals):
        ax.annotate(f"{v:+.1f} dB", (b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, v), xytext=(0, 4 if v >= 0 else -12),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK)
    ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_title("Quality gain on held-out mixtures"); ax.set_ylabel("SI-SDR improvement (dB, median)")
    ax = axes[1]
    groups = ["Handling-noise frames", "Background-only frames"]
    x = np.arange(len(groups)); w = 0.34
    er = stats["energy_removed_db"]
    for i, (name, color, label) in enumerate((("model", MODEL, "Kip model"), ("gate", GATE, "Spectral gate"))):
        v = [er[f"{name}_handling"], er[f"{name}_background"]]
        bs = ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * w, v, width=w, color=color, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=2, label=label)
        for b, val in zip(bs, v):
            ax.annotate(f"{val:.1f}", (b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, val), xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK)
    ax.set_xticks(x, groups); ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8)

def mixture_example(model, src):

    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)

    n = min(len(clip.x), 6 * RATE)

    md += [f"| `{k}` | {v['seconds']} s | {v['flagged_events']} | {v['flagged_s']} s | {v['mean_energy_removed_db']} dB |" for k, v in takes.items()]
    md += ["", "## Training", "", "![training](training.png)", "", "## Suppression compared", "", "![suppression](suppression.png)", "",
           "## A held-out mixture with ground truth", "", "![waveforms](mixture_waveforms.png)", "", "![spectrograms](mixture_spectrograms.png)", "",

"""Charts and listening examples for a trained HandlingNet.

    uv run python -m kipml.report [--checkpoint ...] [--run ml/runs/<latest>] [--n 150]

Writes to ml/reports/handling-poc/:
  training.png               loss curves from the training run
  suppression.png            quality gain and how much each method removes, model vs spectral gate
  mixture_waveforms.png      a held-out mixture with ground truth: waveforms and detection
  mixture_spectrograms.png   the same mixture as spectrograms: input, model, gate, true background
  real_<take>.png            our held-out real takes: before, after, what was removed
  audio/*.wav                before and after files to listen to
  REPORT.md                  the numbers and the charts
Colours follow the dataviz reference palette (validated): blue = model, orange = spectral gate,
aqua = true background (always text-labelled), grey = input.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, json
from pathlib import Path

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
import numpy as np

from .audio import AUDIO, HOP, ML_ROOT, RATE, frame_db, read_wav, write_wav
from .data import Clip, _crop, load_sources, make_example
from .evaluate import load_model, si_sdr, spectral_gate
from .infer import segments
from .model import enhance, stft

SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e6e5e1"
MODEL, GATE, TRUTH, INPUT = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#8a8984"
SEQ = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("blue_seq", [SURFACE, "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"])
OUT = ML_ROOT / "reports" / "handling-poc"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "text.color": INK, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
    "axes.titlesize": 10.5, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "axes.titlelocation": "left", "font.size": 9, "legend.frameon": False,
})


def _envelope(ax, x, color, label=None):
    """Min/max envelope per 10 ms: readable at any length, unlike plotting every sample."""
    n = len(x) // HOP
    seg = x[: n * HOP].reshape(n, HOP)
    t = np.arange(n) * HOP / RATE
    ax.fill_between(t, seg.min(1), seg.max(1), color=color, linewidth=0, label=label)
    ax.set_xlim(0, len(x) / RATE)


def _spec_db(x):
    mag = stft(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(x))[None]).abs()[0].numpy().T
    return 20 * np.log10(mag + 1e-6)


def _spectrogram(ax, x, title, vmax):
    ax.imshow(_spec_db(x), origin="lower", aspect="auto", cmap=SEQ, vmin=vmax - 70, vmax=vmax,
              extent=[0, len(x) / RATE, 0, RATE / 2000])
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_ylabel("kHz"); ax.grid(False)


def training_chart(run_dir: Path):
    hist = json.load(open(run_dir / "metrics.json"))["history"]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax = axes[0]
    for key, color, name in (("train", MODEL, "train"), ("val", GATE, "held-out")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=color, linewidth=1.8, label=name)
        ax.annotate(name, (steps[-1], hist[-1][key]), xytext=(4, 0), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, va="center")
    ax.set_title("Total loss"); ax.set_xlabel("training step"); ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    for ax, key, title in ((axes[1], "val_spec", "Suppression loss (held-out)"), (axes[2], "val_frame_bce", "Detection loss (held-out)")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=MODEL, linewidth=1.8)
        ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xlabel("training step")
    for ax in axes:
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    fig.suptitle("HandlingNet training: loss falls on mixtures it never trained on", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "training.png", dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def suppression_stats(model, src, n):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    imp = {"model": [], "gate": []}
    red = {("model", "handling"): [], ("model", "background"): [], ("gate", "handling"): [], ("gate", "background"): []}
    tp = fp = fn = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        mix, clean, labels, has = make_example(rng, src, "test", 4.0)
        out, prob = enhance(model, mix)
        gate = spectral_gate(mix)
        f_in = frame_db(mix)
        lab = labels.astype(bool) if has else np.zeros(len(f_in), bool)
        for name, y in (("model", out), ("gate", gate)):
            drop = f_in - frame_db(y)
            if lab.any():
                red[(name, "handling")].append(float(np.mean(drop[lab])))
            if (~lab).any():
                red[(name, "background")].append(float(np.mean(drop[~lab])))
        if has:
            base = si_sdr(mix, clean)
            imp["model"].append(si_sdr(out, clean) - base)
            imp["gate"].append(si_sdr(gate, clean) - base)
            pred = prob[: len(lab)] > 0.5
            tp += int((pred & lab).sum()); fp += int((pred & ~lab).sum()); fn += int((~pred & lab).sum())
    prec, rec = tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
    return {"si_sdr_improvement_db": {k: round(float(np.median(v)), 2) for k, v in imp.items()},
            "energy_removed_db": {f"{m}_{k}": round(float(np.mean(v)), 2) for (m, k), v in red.items()},
            "detection": {"precision": round(prec, 3), "recall": round(rec, 3), "f1": round(2 * prec * rec / max(prec + rec, 1e-9), 3)},
            "mixtures": n}

        for b, val in zip(bs, v):

toolUseResult.content:
"""Charts and listening examples for a trained HandlingNet.

    uv run python -m kipml.report [--checkpoint ...] [--run ml/runs/<latest>] [--n 150]

Writes to ml/reports/handling-poc/:
  training.png               loss curves from the training run
  suppression.png            quality gain and how much each method removes, model vs spectral gate
  mixture_waveforms.png      a held-out mixture with ground truth: waveforms and detection
  mixture_spectrograms.png   the same mixture as spectrograms: input, model, gate, true background
  real_<take>.png            our held-out real takes: before, after, what was removed
  audio/*.wav                before and after files to listen to
  REPORT.md                  the numbers and the charts
Colours follow the dataviz reference palette (validated): blue = model, orange = spectral gate,
aqua = true background (always text-labelled), grey = input.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
import numpy as np
import torch

from .audio import AUDIO, HOP, ML_ROOT, RATE, frame_db, read_wav, write_wav
from .data import Clip, _crop, load_sources, make_example
from .evaluate import load_model, si_sdr, spectral_gate
from .infer import segments
from .model import enhance, stft

SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e6e5e1"
MODEL, GATE, TRUTH, INPUT = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#8a8984"
SEQ = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("blue_seq", [SURFACE, "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"])
OUT = ML_ROOT / "reports" / "handling-poc"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "text.color": INK, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
    "axes.titlesize": 10.5, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "axes.titlelocation": "left", "font.size": 9, "legend.frameon": False,
})


def _envelope(ax, x, color, label=None):
    """Min/max envelope per 10 ms: readable at any length, unlike plotting every sample."""
    n = len(x) // HOP
    seg = x[: n * HOP].reshape(n, HOP)
    t = np.arange(n) * HOP / RATE
    ax.fill_between(t, seg.min(1), seg.max(1), color=color, linewidth=0, label=label)
    ax.set_xlim(0, len(x) / RATE)


def _spec_db(x):
    mag = stft(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(x))[None]).abs()[0].numpy().T
    return 20 * np.log10(mag + 1e-6)


def _spectrogram(ax, x, title, vmax):
    ax.imshow(_spec_db(x), origin="lower", aspect="auto", cmap=SEQ, vmin=vmax - 70, vmax=vmax,
              extent=[0, len(x) / RATE, 0, RATE / 2000])
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_ylabel("kHz"); ax.grid(False)


def training_chart(run_dir: Path):
    hist = json.load(open(run_dir / "metrics.json"))["history"]
    steps = [h["step"] for h in hist]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax = axes[0]
    for key, color, name in (("train", MODEL, "train"), ("val", GATE, "held-out")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=color, linewidth=1.8, label=name)
        ax.annotate(name, (steps[-1], hist[-1][key]), xytext=(4, 0), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, va="center")
    ax.set_title("Total loss"); ax.set_xlabel("training step"); ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    for ax, key, title in ((axes[1], "val_spec", "Suppression loss (held-out)"), (axes[2], "val_frame_bce", "Detection loss (held-out)")):
        ax.plot(steps, [h[key] for h in hist], color=MODEL, linewidth=1.8)
        ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xlabel("training step")
    for ax in axes:
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    fig.suptitle("HandlingNet training: loss falls on mixtures it never trained on", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "training.png", dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def suppression_stats(model, src, n):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    imp = {"model": [], "gate": []}
    red = {("model", "handling"): [], ("model", "background"): [], ("gate", "handling"): [], ("gate", "background"): []}
    tp = fp = fn = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        mix, clean, labels, has = make_example(rng, src, "test", 4.0)
        out, prob = enhance(model, mix)
        gate = spectral_gate(mix)
        f_in = frame_db(mix)
        lab = labels.astype(bool) if has else np.zeros(len(f_in), bool)
        for name, y in (("model", out), ("gate", gate)):
            drop = f_in - frame_db(y)
            if lab.any():
                red[(name, "handling")].append(float(np.mean(drop[lab])))
            if (~lab).any():
                red[(name, "background")].append(float(np.mean(drop[~lab])))
        if has:
            base = si_sdr(mix, clean)
            imp["model"].append(si_sdr(out, clean) - base)
            imp["gate"].append(si_sdr(gate, clean) - base)
            pred = prob[: len(lab)] > 0.5
            tp += int((pred & lab).sum()); fp += int((pred & ~lab).sum()); fn += int((~pred & lab).sum())
    prec, rec = tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
    return {"si_sdr_improvement_db": {k: round(float(np.median(v)), 2) for k, v in imp.items()},
            "energy_removed_db": {f"{m}_{k}": round(float(np.mean(v)), 2) for (m, k), v in red.items()},
            "detection": {"precision": round(prec, 3), "recall": round(rec, 3), "f1": round(2 * prec * rec / max(prec + rec, 1e-9), 3)},
            "mixtures": n}


def suppression_chart(stats):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.6), constrained_layout=True)
    ax = axes[0]
    vals = [stats["si_sdr_improvement_db"]["model"], stats["si_sdr_improvement_db"]["gate"]]
    bars = ax.bar(["Kip model", "Spectral gate"], vals, color=[MODEL, GATE], width=0.5, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=2)
    for b, v in zip(bars, vals):
        ax.annotate(f"{v:+.1f} dB", (b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, v), xytext=(0, 4 if v >= 0 else -12),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK)
    ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_title("Quality gain on held-out mixtures"); ax.set_ylabel("SI-SDR improvement (dB, median)")
    ax = axes[1]
    groups = ["Handling-noise frames", "Background-only frames"]
    x = np.arange(len(groups)); w = 0.34
    er = stats["energy_removed_db"]
    for i, (name, color, label) in enumerate((("model", MODEL, "Kip model"), ("gate", GATE, "Spectral gate"))):
        v = [er[f"{name}_handling"], er[f"{name}_background"]]
        bs = ax.bar(x + (i - 0.5) * w, v, width=w, color=color, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=2, label=label)
        for b, val in zip(bs, v):
            ax.annotate(f"{val:.1f}", (b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, val), xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK)
    ax.set_xticks(x, groups); ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_title("How much each method removes"); ax.set_ylabel("energy removed (dB, mean)")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    fig.suptitle("Kip removes handling noise and leaves the rest; a noise gate cannot tell them apart",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "suppression.png", dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def mixture_example(model, src):
    """A held-out mixture built from one of our real test takes, with its true background."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    ours = src["handling"]["test"]["ours"]
    clip = next(c for c in ours if "pickup" in c.name)
    bg_clip = next(c for c in src["background"]["test"] if "traffic" in c.name or "engine" in c.name) if any(
        "engine" in c.name for c in src["background"]["test"]) else src["background"]["test"][0]
    n = min(len(clip.x), 6 * RATE)
    h, _ = _crop(rng, clip.x, n)
    bg, _ = _crop(rng, bg_clip.x, n)
    h *= np.sqrt(np.mean(bg ** 2) * 10 ** (5 / 10) / (np.mean(h ** 2) + 1e-12))
    mix = bg + h
    g = 0.3 / (np.abs(mix).max() + 1e-9)
    mix, bg = (mix * g).astype(np.float32), (bg * g).astype(np.float32)
    labels = frame_db(h) > clip.floor_db + 8
    out, prob = enhance(model, mix)
    gate = spectral_gate(mix)
    scores = {k: si_sdr(y, bg) for k, y in (("input", mix), ("model", out), ("gate", gate))}

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(5, 1, figsize=(11, 8.2), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True,
                             gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1, 1, 1, 1, 0.9]})
    lim = np.abs(mix).max() * 1.05
    for ax, y, color, title in ((axes[0], mix, INPUT, f"Input: background plus our real drop take ({scores['input']:.1f} dB SI-SDR)"),
                                (axes[1], out, MODEL, f"Kip model output ({scores['model']:.1f} dB)"),
                                (axes[2], gate, GATE, f"Spectral gate output ({scores['gate']:.1f} dB)"),
                                (axes[3], bg, TRUTH, "True background (what a perfect filter returns)")):
        _envelope(ax, y, color); ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim); ax.set_title(title); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax = axes[4]
    t = np.arange(len(prob)) * HOP / RATE
    for s, e in segments(labels.astype(float), 0.5):
        ax.axvspan(s, e, color=GRID, linewidth=0)
    ax.plot(t, prob, color=MODEL, linewidth=1.5)
    ax.axhline(0.5, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8, linestyle=(0, (3, 3)))
    ax.annotate("threshold 0.5", (t[-1], 0.5), xytext=(-4, 4), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=INK2)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1); ax.set_title("Handling probability per 10 ms (grey bands: where handling noise really is)")
    ax.set_xlabel("seconds")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "mixture_waveforms.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)

    vmax = _spec_db(mix).max()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(11, 8), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, y, title in ((axes[0], mix, "Input"), (axes[1], out, "Kip model output"),
                         (axes[2], gate, "Spectral gate output"), (axes[3], bg, "True background")):
        _spectrogram(ax, y, title, vmax)
    axes[-1].set_xlabel("seconds")
    fig.suptitle("Spectrograms (darker = louder, same scale): the model erases the broadband bursts",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "mixture_spectrograms.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)
    for name, y in (("mixture_input", mix), ("mixture_kip", out), ("mixture_gate", gate), ("mixture_true_background", bg)):
        write_wav(OUT / "audio" / f"{name}.wav", y)
    return {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in scores.items()}


def real_take(model, path: Path):
    x = read_wav(path)
    out, prob = enhance(model, x)
    removed = x - out
    segs = segments(prob, 0.5)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(6, 1, figsize=(11, 10), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True,
                             gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1, 1, 1, 0.8, 1.3, 1.3]})
    lim = np.abs(x).max() * 1.05
    for ax, y, color, title in ((axes[0], x, INPUT, "Recorded on the iPhone (held out: never trained on)"),
                                (axes[1], out, MODEL, "After the Kip model"),
                                (axes[2], removed, GATE, "What the model removed")):
        _envelope(ax, y, color); ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim); ax.set_title(title); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax = axes[3]
    ax.plot(np.arange(len(prob)) * HOP / RATE, prob, color=MODEL, linewidth=1.5)
    ax.axhline(0.5, color=INK2, linewidth=0.8, linestyle=(0, (3, 3)))
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1); ax.set_title(f"Handling probability: {len(segs)} events flagged, {sum(e - s for s, e in segs):.1f} s in total")
    vmax = _spec_db(x).max()
    _spectrogram(axes[4], x, "Spectrogram before", vmax)
    _spectrogram(axes[5], out, "Spectrogram after", vmax)
    axes[-1].set_xlabel("seconds")
    fig.suptitle(f"{path.stem}: real phone-handling noise, before and after", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(OUT / f"real_{path.stem}.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)
    write_wav(OUT / "audio" / f"{path.stem}_input.wav", x)
    write_wav(OUT / "audio" / f"{path.stem}_kip.wav", out)
    reduction = float(np.mean(frame_db(x) - frame_db(out)))
    return {"seconds": round(len(x) / RATE, 1), "flagged_events": len(segs), "flagged_s": round(sum(e - s for s, e in segs), 1),
            "mean_energy_removed_db": round(reduction, 1)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint", default=str(ML_ROOT / "checkpoints" / "handling-poc.pt"))
    ap.add_argument("--run", help="training run dir (default: latest with metrics.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=150)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    (OUT / "audio").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    run = Path(args.run) if args.run else max((p.parent for p in (ML_ROOT / "runs").glob("*/metrics.json")), key=lambda p: p.name)
    model, src = load_model(args.checkpoint), load_sources()
    training_chart(run)
    stats = suppression_stats(model, src, args.n)
    suppression_chart(stats)
    example = mixture_example(model, src)
    takes = {p.stem: real_take(model, p) for p in sorted((AUDIO / "ours").glob("*.wav"))
             if any(t in p.name for t in ("sleeve_03", "pickup_01", "pocket_02"))}
    summary = {"run": run.name, **stats, "mixture_example_si_sdr_db": example, "real_takes": takes}
    (OUT / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=1))
    hist = json.load(open(run / "metrics.json"))["history"]
    md = ["# HandlingNet proof of concept", "",
          f"Trained {hist[-1]['step']} steps ({hist[-1]['secs'] // 60} min on an M1 Pro CPU). Every number below is on "
          "audio the model never trained on. Regenerate with `uv run python -m kipml.report`.", "",
          "| Metric | Kip model | Spectral gate |", "|---|---|---|",
          f"| SI-SDR improvement, median ({stats['mixtures']} mixtures) | {stats['si_sdr_improvement_db']['model']:+.1f} dB | {stats['si_sdr_improvement_db']['gate']:+.1f} dB |",
          f"| Energy removed on handling-noise frames | {stats['energy_removed_db']['model_handling']:.1f} dB | {stats['energy_removed_db']['gate_handling']:.1f} dB |",
          f"| Energy removed on background-only frames | {stats['energy_removed_db']['model_background']:.1f} dB | {stats['energy_removed_db']['gate_background']:.1f} dB |",
          f"| Handling-frame detection (precision / recall / F1) | {stats['detection']['precision']:.2f} / {stats['detection']['recall']:.2f} / {stats['detection']['f1']:.2f} | n/a |", "",
          "Real held-out takes from the iPhone:", "", "| Take | Length | Events flagged | Flagged time | Energy removed |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    md += [f"| `{k}` | {v['seconds']} s | {v['flagged_events']} | {v['flagged_s']} s | {v['mean_energy_removed_db']} dB |" for k, v in takes.items()]
    md += ["", "## Training", "", "![training](training.png)", "", "## Suppression compared", "", "![suppression](suppression.png)", "",
           "## A held-out mixture with ground truth", "", "![waveforms](mixture_waveforms.png)", "", "![spectrograms](mixture_spectrograms.png)", "",
           "## Real takes from the phone", ""] + [f"![{k}](real_{k}.png)\n" for k in takes] + [
           "## Listen", "", "Before and after files are in `audio/`: `mixture_input.wav`, `mixture_kip.wav`, `mixture_gate.wav`, "
           "`mixture_true_background.wav`, and `<take>_input.wav` / `<take>_kip.wav` for each real take.", ""]
    (OUT / "REPORT.md").write_text("\n".join(md))

    from kipml.data import frames_to_samples

# Lium — Python SDK & CLI
## Installation
### Python package
### Binary install (macOS amd64/arm64 / Linux amd64/arm64)
## Quick Start
### CLI
# First-time setup: create an account (mints and stores an API key) …
# … or link an existing account (opens a browser). Headless (agents, CI, containers): pass the key
# instead — lium init --api-key sk_...   (keys: https://lium.io/api-keys), or export LIUM_API_KEY and skip init.
lium init
lium balance
# List available nodes (GPU machines)
lium ls
# Price a job on node #1 before renting it (no API key needed)
# Create a pod using node index
lium up 1  # Use node #1 from previous ls
# Or create a pod using filters
lium up --gpu A100  # Auto-select best A100 node
# List your pods
lium ps
lium ps --filter status=RUNNING --sort spent   # running pods, most expensive so far first
lium spend                                     # burn per hour, spend per pod, runway
# Copy files to pod
lium scp 1 ./my_script.py
# SSH into a pod
lium ssh <pod-name>
# Stop a pod — billing is per second and runs until you do this
lium rm <pod-name>
### First hour on a pod
- Always pass `--ttl` (or `--until`) to `lium up`; a pod bills until it is removed.
### SDK
High-level decorator — annotate a function and offload work to a GPU pod. `machine` is `"<count>x<gpu>"` or `"<gpu>"` (`"1xH200"`, `"A100"`, `"2xRTX4090"`; count defaults to 1; the GPU is named as `lium ls --gpu` takes it and matched whole, so `"A100"` never rents an RTX A1000) and the cheapest matching node is rented; `timeout=` (default 1 h) bounds the run and the pod's lifetime. Arguments travel as a pickle (your own bytes, loaded on your own pod); the result comes back as a JSON envelope plus an `.npz` sidecar for numpy arrays read with `allow_pickle=False`, so nothing the pod writes is unpickled on your machine. What round-trips: `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float`/`str`/`bytes`, `list`/`tuple`/`set`/`frozenset`/`dict` of those, `datetime`/`date`/`time`/`timedelta`, `Decimal`, `pathlib.Path`, `uuid.UUID`, `numpy.ndarray` (any dtype without Python objects) and numpy scalars — anything else is a `lium.ResultEncodingError` on the pod naming the type (return `.tolist()`, `dict(x)`, `x.value` instead). Only the function's own `def` is sent, so import inside it and pass everything else as arguments. A remote exception is re-raised with its type when that type is a builtin (`except ValueError` works; other types arrive as `lium.RemoteExecutionError` with the name), with `lium.RemoteExecutionError` (remote traceback, exit code, output) as its cause:
`keep_warm=300` keeps the pod five minutes for the next call or the next run of the script; `infer.map(prompts)` runs every item on one pod; `infer.local(...)` runs the function here (`local=True` / `LIUM_MACHINE_LOCAL=1` does so for every call); `infer.close()` removes a warm pod. Progress goes to stderr (`quiet=True` to silence):
# the cheapest available 1×A100 with at least 32 CPUs, chosen and rented in one call
print(f"{rented.executor.huid} at ${rented.price_per_hour:.2f}/h")
`wait_ready()` raises `PodStartError` — with `.pod`, `.status`, `.history` and `.cause` (what the backend recorded, e.g. `Container creation failed due to ... (failure_step: ssh_connect)`) — when the pod reaches `FAILED`/`CREATION_FAILED`/`STOPPED`/`BROKEN` or disappears from the pod list, so a dead pod is not mistaken for a slow one. Pass `on_poll=lambda pod, status, elapsed: ...` to be told about every poll. `lium up` is bounded by `--timeout SECONDS` (default 900) for the whole rent, prints `waiting for <pod>… <STATUS> (<n> s)` while it waits, and exits 1 naming the pod when the budget runs out; `--ready-timeout` caps only the wait.
# later: lium.down(pod)
# later, from another process or agent turn:
is gone). `lium ps --format json` and `lium describe` (table and `--json`) show the same command
## Documentation
- **Exit codes and the JSON error envelope:** [docs/exit-codes.md](docs/exit-codes.md) — what a script or agent gets back when a command fails (`--format json`, `LIUM_OUTPUT=json`).
## Binary Releases
## CLI Reference
### Core Commands
- `lium signup` - Create an account from the terminal and store its API key (`--totp-code` answers a two-factor sign-in)
- `lium init` - Initialize configuration for an existing account (API key, SSH keys); `--api-key <key>` for machines without a browser; `--force` to log in again
- `lium balance` - Show the account balance (add `--format json` for machine-readable output)
- `lium whoami` - Show which API key is in use, where it came from, and the account it belongs to
- `lium ls [--gpu TYPE] [--count N] [--country CODE] [--min-vram GB] [--max-price USD] [--tier spot|secure] [--format json]` - List available nodes
- `lium up [NODE_ID]` - Create a pod (NODE_ID is the HUID or UUID from `lium ls`, or its row number; or use filters like `--gpu`, `--count`, `--country`; cap it with `--ttl 6h` or `--budget 12.50`; `--json` prints the ready pod as JSON instead of opening SSH)
- `lium ps [--sort KEY] [--filter KEY=VALUE] [--key NAME|ID] [--watch N] [--wide] [--format json]` - List active pods; the `#` column is the row number `rm`/`ssh`/`exec`/`scp` accept in the same shell, for 10 minutes, and only while the pod shown on that row is still listed — the rows of the last listing, in the order shown (sorted or filtered). Use the huid in scripts. A PENDING pod gets a line under the table with the backend's start estimate and phase, worded as `lium up` words it (`eager-wolf-aa PENDING · est. ready in ~18 s (phase: pulling image)`); its `--format json` row carries the same text as `eta_hint` (`null` when the backend sent neither).
- `lium quote <node> --hours N [--gpus N] [--volume-gb N] [--backup-gb N] [--format json]` - A job's compute, volume and backup cost on a node at billing's rates, before renting
- `lium ssh <POD>` - SSH into a pod
- `lium exec <POD> <COMMAND>` - Execute command on pod (`--json` for stdout/stderr/exit_code; `-d/--detach` starts it in the background and returns immediately; `--max-output-bytes N` sets the output limit, default 64 MiB)
- `lium scp <POD> <LOCAL_FILE> [REMOTE_PATH]` - Copy files to pods (add `-d` to download from pods)
- `lium rsync <POD> <LOCAL_DIR> [REMOTE_PATH]` - Sync directories to pods (`--bwlimit`, `--exclude`, `--delete`, `--progress`; resumes on re-run)
- `lium rm <POD>` - Remove/stop a pod (`--name-only` to refuse `lium ps` row numbers in scripts; `--format json` prints what was removed with its estimated spend; `--rating 1-5 --feedback "..."` rates the node in the same call)
- `lium reset-gpu <POD> [--gpu N ...]` - Reset a pod's hung GPUs; stops the pod's processes, keeps its files; waits 1-2 min for the result
- `lium gpu-clocks <POD> --lock MIN,MAX | --reset [--gpu N ...]` - Lock a pod's GPU core clocks to a MHz range, or reset them to the default; the pod keeps running
- `lium audit [--pod POD] [--since 24h] [--key ID]` - Who did what to the account's pods, and when: every rent, reboot, edit and delete with the session or API key that requested it (add `--json` for machine-readable output)

import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
md, code = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell, nbf.v4.new_code_cell
cells = []

cells.append(md("""# Kip handling-noise filter: proof of concept

A phone on a nightstand, in a pocket or under a pillow hears **itself**: fabric rubbing on the mic, the phone being
knocked or set down. Those spikes would otherwise be labelled and linked to wake-ups. **HandlingNet** is a small model
we trained ourselves (about 0.2 to 0.4M parameters) that flags phone-handling noise every 10 ms and removes it,
while leaving the room alone.

This notebook shows the data, the training, how it compares with a classic spectral noise gate, and what it does to
real recordings from our demo iPhone. **Every number is measured on audio the model never trained on.**

- Code: `ml/kipml/` (data, model, train, evaluate, infer, export, report) and `ml/README.md`
- Charts and before/after audio: `ml/reports/`
- To run it yourself: `cd ml && uv sync --group dev && uv run jupyter lab notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb`
  (or open it in VS Code with the `ml/.venv` kernel)."""))

cells.append(code("""import json, sys
from pathlib import Path

ML = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "kipml").is_dir())
sys.path.insert(0, str(ML))

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Audio, Image, Markdown, display

from kipml import report                      # applies the chart style (validated palette)
from kipml.audio import AUDIO, HOP, RATE, read_wav
from kipml.data import load_sources, make_example
from kipml.evaluate import load_model
from kipml.model import enhance, count_params
%matplotlib inline

REPORTS = {name: ML / "reports" / name for name in ("handling-poc", "handling-gpu") if (ML / "reports" / name / "summary.json").exists()}
print("reports found:", ", ".join(REPORTS) or "none: run `uv run python -m kipml.report` first")"""))

cells.append(md("""## 1. The data

Training examples are **mixed on the fly**: a 2 to 4 second slice of a night background, plus (75% of the time) a
slice of phone-handling noise at a random loudness (-5 to +20 dB against the background), then a random overall
gain. That turns a few minutes of recordings into unlimited, always-different examples.

**Labels**: a 10 ms frame counts as handling noise when the handling clip is louder there than its own quiet floor
by 8 dB and, for our venue takes, louder than the venue itself (90th percentile of the venue room tone plus 3 dB).
**Target**: the background plus the quiet parts of the take, so the model learns to remove the bursts, not the room.

Splits are by source file: three of our takes (`sleeve_03`, `pickup_01`, `pocket_02`), the last four placeholder
clips, ESC-50 fold 5 and the last 20% of the private room recordings are never trained on."""))

cells.append(code("""src = load_sources()
rows = []
for group, splits in (("handling", src["handling"]), ("background", src["background"])):
    for split, clips in splits.items():
        pools = clips if isinstance(clips, dict) else {"all": clips}
        for pool, cs in pools.items():
            secs = sum(len(c.x) for c in cs) / RATE
            rows.append(f"| {group} | {pool} | {split} | {len(cs)} | {secs:.0f} s |")
display(Markdown("| Kind | Source | Split | Clips | Audio |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(rows)))"""))

cells.append(code("""# One training example, exactly as the model sees it
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
while True:
    mix, target, labels, has = make_example(rng, src, "train", seconds=4.0)
    if has and 0.05 < labels.mean() < 0.6:
        break
t = np.arange(len(mix)) / RATE
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(11, 5.5), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True)
report._envelope(axes[0], mix, report.INPUT); axes[0].set_title("Mixture: what the phone hears"); axes[0].set_yticks([])
report._envelope(axes[1], target, report.TRUTH); axes[1].set_title("Target: background plus the take's quiet parts (green)"); axes[1].set_yticks([])
lim = np.abs(mix).max() * 1.05
for ax in axes[:2]:
    ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
axes[2].fill_between(np.arange(len(labels)) * HOP / RATE, 0, labels, color=report.MODEL, step="mid", linewidth=0)
axes[2].set_ylim(0, 1.05); axes[2].set_yticks([0, 1], ["room", "handling"]); axes[2].set_title("Label per 10 ms frame")
axes[2].set_xlabel("seconds")
plt.show()
display(Audio(mix, rate=RATE))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 2. Training

The loss has two parts: how close the cleaned spectrogram is to the target (**suppression**), and how well the
model flags handling frames (**detection**). *Held-out* is a fixed set of mixtures built only from test sources."""))

cells.append(code("""for name, folder in REPORTS.items():
    display(Markdown(f"**{name}**"))
    display(Image(filename=str(folder / "training.png")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 3. Against a classic spectral noise gate

A spectral gate estimates a steady noise floor per frequency and subtracts it. It is the standard tool for
"remove background noise", and the wrong tool here: handling noise is short and bursty, so a gate barely touches
it while still eating into the room. **SI-SDR improvement** measures how much closer the output gets to the target
(higher is better); the right-hand chart shows how much each method removes where there *is* handling noise and
where there is *not* (ideal: a lot, then nothing)."""))

cells.append(code("""def row(name, s):
    e, d = s["energy_removed_db"], s["detection"]
    return (f"| {name} | {s['si_sdr_improvement_db']['model']:+.1f} dB | {s['si_sdr_improvement_db']['gate']:+.1f} dB | "
            f"{e['model_handling']:.1f} / {e['model_background']:.1f} dB | {e['gate_handling']:.1f} / {e['gate_background']:.1f} dB | "
            f"{d['precision']:.2f} / {d['recall']:.2f} / {d['f1']:.2f} |")
summaries = {name: json.loads((f / "summary.json").read_text()) for name, f in REPORTS.items()}
display(Markdown("| Model | SI-SDR gain, model | SI-SDR gain, gate | Removed by model (handling / room) | Removed by gate (handling / room) | Detection P / R / F1 |\\n"
                 "|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(row(n, s) for n, s in summaries.items())))
for name, folder in REPORTS.items():
    display(Markdown(f"**{name}**")); display(Image(filename=str(folder / "suppression.png")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 4. One held-out mixture, with the true answer

One of our real drop takes (held out) mixed into a held-out background. Compare the model's output with the gate's
and with the target. Listen below: input, model, gate, target."""))

cells.append(code("""best = "handling-gpu" if "handling-gpu" in REPORTS else "handling-poc"
folder = REPORTS[best]
display(Markdown(f"Model: **{best}**"))
display(Image(filename=str(folder / "mixture_waveforms.png")))
display(Image(filename=str(folder / "mixture_spectrograms.png")))
for name in ("mixture_input", "mixture_kip", "mixture_gate", "mixture_true_background"):
    display(Markdown(f"`{name}`")); display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / f"{name}.wav")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 5. Real takes from the demo iPhone (held out)

No synthetic mixing here: the raw recordings, scored against the same label rule used in training (grey bands:
moments louder than the venue). Precision and recall are per 10 ms frame."""))

cells.append(code("""rows = []
for name, s in summaries.items():
    for take, v in s["real_takes"].items():
        rows.append(f"| {name} | `{take}` | {v['handling_s']} s | {v['flagged_s']} s | {v['precision']} / {v['recall']} | "
                    f"{v['removed_on_handling_db']} dB | {v['removed_elsewhere_db']} dB |")
display(Markdown("| Model | Take | Handling (label) | Flagged | Precision / recall | Removed on handling | Removed elsewhere |\\n"
                 "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(rows)))
for png in sorted(folder.glob("real_*.png")):
    display(Image(filename=str(png)))
display(Markdown("Listen: `venue_pickup_01` before, then after"))
display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / "venue_pickup_01_input.wav")))
display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / "venue_pickup_01_kip.wav")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 6. Try it on any recording

Point this at any file from any device (an iPhone Voice Memo `.m4a` works): it prints the flagged moments and
writes `<name>.clean.wav` next to it. Same as `uv run python -m kipml.infer <file>` from the `ml/` folder."""))

cells.append(code("""from kipml.audio import load_any
from kipml.infer import segments

checkpoint = ML / "checkpoints" / ("handling-gpu.pt" if (ML / "checkpoints" / "handling-gpu.pt").exists() else "handling-poc.pt")
model = load_model(checkpoint)
print(f"{checkpoint.name}: {count_params(model):,} parameters")

recording = AUDIO / "ours" / "venue_pickup_02.wav"      # <- change me (this take was used in training)
x = load_any(recording)
clean, prob = enhance(model, x)
for s, e in segments(prob, 0.5, min_s=0.03):
    print(f"handling {s:6.2f} to {e:6.2f} s")
display(Audio(x, rate=RATE)); display(Audio(clean, rate=RATE))"""))

cells.append(md("""## Limits, honestly

- **Small, single-venue data**: about 3 minutes of real handling noise from one phone in one noisy hall, plus
  synthetic placeholders and ESC-50 backgrounds. Expect it to be best on that phone and that kind of room.
- **Detection is the strong part.** On the held-out drop take it flags the five drops and almost nothing else.
  Suppression on raw takes is modest; flagging the frame is what Kip needs (a flagged spike is never linked to a
  wake-up), and cleaner removal needs more and more varied recordings.
- **Quiet handling is not labelled**: sleeve rubbing that is not louder than the venue counts as room, by design.
- **Licences**: ESC-50 is CC BY-NC 3.0, fine for this prototype only. Our recordings were speech-checked before
  committing; recordings with other people's conversation never leave our machines."""))

nb.cells = cells
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {"name": "python3", "display_name": "Python 3 (ml/.venv)", "language": "python"}
nbf.write(nb, "notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb")
print("written", len(cells), "cells")

import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
md, code = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell, nbf.v4.new_code_cell
cells = []

cells.append(md("""# Kip handling-noise filter: proof of concept

A phone on a nightstand, in a pocket or under a pillow hears **itself**: fabric rubbing on the mic, the phone being
knocked or set down. Those spikes would otherwise be labelled and linked to wake-ups. **HandlingNet** is a small model
we trained ourselves (about 0.2 to 0.4M parameters) that flags phone-handling noise every 10 ms and removes it,
while leaving the room alone.

This notebook shows the data, the training, how it compares with a classic spectral noise gate, and what it does to
real recordings from our demo iPhone. **Every number is measured on audio the model never trained on.**

- Code: `ml/kipml/` (data, model, train, evaluate, infer, export, report) and `ml/README.md`
- Charts and before/after audio: `ml/reports/`
- To run it yourself: `cd ml && uv sync --group dev && uv run jupyter lab notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb`
  (or open it in VS Code with the `ml/.venv` kernel)."""))

cells.append(code("""import json, sys
from pathlib import Path

ML = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "kipml").is_dir())
sys.path.insert(0, str(ML))

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Audio, Image, Markdown, display

from kipml import report                      # applies the chart style (validated palette)
from kipml.audio import AUDIO, HOP, RATE, read_wav
from kipml.data import load_sources, make_example
from kipml.evaluate import load_model
from kipml.model import enhance, count_params
%matplotlib inline

REPORTS = {name: ML / "reports" / name for name in ("handling-poc", "handling-gpu") if (ML / "reports" / name / "summary.json").exists()}
print("reports found:", ", ".join(REPORTS) or "none: run `uv run python -m kipml.report` first")"""))

cells.append(md("""## 1. The data

Training examples are **mixed on the fly**: a 2 to 4 second slice of a night background, plus (75% of the time) a
slice of phone-handling noise at a random loudness (-5 to +20 dB against the background), then a random overall
gain. That turns a few minutes of recordings into unlimited, always-different examples.

**Labels**: a 10 ms frame counts as handling noise when the handling clip is louder there than its own quiet floor
by 8 dB and, for our venue takes, louder than the venue itself (90th percentile of the venue room tone plus 3 dB).
**Target**: the background plus the quiet parts of the take, so the model learns to remove the bursts, not the room.

Splits are by source file: three of our takes (`sleeve_03`, `pickup_01`, `pocket_02`), the last four placeholder
clips, ESC-50 fold 5 and the last 20% of the private room recordings are never trained on."""))

cells.append(code("""src = load_sources()
rows = []
for group, splits in (("handling", src["handling"]), ("background", src["background"])):
    for split, clips in splits.items():
        pools = clips if isinstance(clips, dict) else {"all": clips}
        for pool, cs in pools.items():
            secs = sum(len(c.x) for c in cs) / RATE
            rows.append(f"| {group} | {pool} | {split} | {len(cs)} | {secs:.0f} s |")
display(Markdown("| Kind | Source | Split | Clips | Audio |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(rows)))"""))

cells.append(code("""# One training example, exactly as the model sees it
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
while True:
    mix, target, labels, has = make_example(rng, src, "train", seconds=4.0)
    if has and 0.05 < labels.mean() < 0.6:
        break
t = np.arange(len(mix)) / RATE
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(11, 5.5), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True)
report._envelope(axes[0], mix, report.INPUT); axes[0].set_title("Mixture: what the phone hears"); axes[0].set_yticks([])
report._envelope(axes[1], target, report.TRUTH); axes[1].set_title("Target: background plus the take's quiet parts (green)"); axes[1].set_yticks([])
lim = np.abs(mix).max() * 1.05
for ax in axes[:2]:
    ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
axes[2].fill_between(np.arange(len(labels)) * HOP / RATE, 0, labels, color=report.MODEL, step="mid", linewidth=0)
axes[2].set_ylim(0, 1.05); axes[2].set_yticks([0, 1], ["room", "handling"]); axes[2].set_title("Label per 10 ms frame")
axes[2].set_xlabel("seconds")
plt.show()
display(Audio(mix, rate=RATE))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 2. Training

The loss has two parts: how close the cleaned spectrogram is to the target (**suppression**), and how well the
model flags handling frames (**detection**). *Held-out* is a fixed set of mixtures built only from test sources."""))

cells.append(code("""for name, folder in REPORTS.items():
    display(Markdown(f"**{name}**"))
    display(Image(filename=str(folder / "training.png")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 3. Against a classic spectral noise gate

A spectral gate estimates a steady noise floor per frequency and subtracts it. It is the standard tool for
"remove background noise", and the wrong tool here: handling noise is short and bursty, so a gate barely touches
it while still eating into the room. **SI-SDR improvement** measures how much closer the output gets to the target
(higher is better); the right-hand chart shows how much each method removes where there *is* handling noise and
where there is *not* (ideal: a lot, then nothing)."""))

cells.append(code("""def row(name, s):
    e, d = s["energy_removed_db"], s["detection"]
    return (f"| {name} | {s['si_sdr_improvement_db']['model']:+.1f} dB | {s['si_sdr_improvement_db']['gate']:+.1f} dB | "
            f"{e['model_handling']:.1f} / {e['model_background']:.1f} dB | {e['gate_handling']:.1f} / {e['gate_background']:.1f} dB | "
            f"{d['precision']:.2f} / {d['recall']:.2f} / {d['f1']:.2f} |")
summaries = {name: json.loads((f / "summary.json").read_text()) for name, f in REPORTS.items()}
display(Markdown("| Model | SI-SDR gain, model | SI-SDR gain, gate | Removed by model (handling / room) | Removed by gate (handling / room) | Detection P / R / F1 |\\n"
                 "|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(row(n, s) for n, s in summaries.items())))
for name, folder in REPORTS.items():
    display(Markdown(f"**{name}**")); display(Image(filename=str(folder / "suppression.png")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 4. One held-out mixture, with the true answer

One of our real drop takes (held out) mixed into a held-out background. Compare the model's output with the gate's
and with the target. Listen below: input, model, gate, target."""))

cells.append(code("""best = "handling-gpu" if "handling-gpu" in REPORTS else "handling-poc"
folder = REPORTS[best]
display(Markdown(f"Model: **{best}**"))
display(Image(filename=str(folder / "mixture_waveforms.png")))
display(Image(filename=str(folder / "mixture_spectrograms.png")))
for name in ("mixture_input", "mixture_kip", "mixture_gate", "mixture_true_background"):
    display(Markdown(f"`{name}`")); display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / f"{name}.wav")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 5. Real takes from the demo iPhone (held out)

No synthetic mixing here: the raw recordings, scored against the same label rule used in training (grey bands:
moments louder than the venue). Precision and recall are per 10 ms frame."""))

cells.append(code("""rows = []
for name, s in summaries.items():
    for take, v in s["real_takes"].items():
        rows.append(f"| {name} | `{take}` | {v['handling_s']} s | {v['flagged_s']} s | {v['precision']} / {v['recall']} | "
                    f"{v['removed_on_handling_db']} dB | {v['removed_elsewhere_db']} dB |")
display(Markdown("| Model | Take | Handling (label) | Flagged | Precision / recall | Removed on handling | Removed elsewhere |\\n"
                 "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n" + "\\n".join(rows)))
for png in sorted(folder.glob("real_*.png")):
    display(Image(filename=str(png)))
display(Markdown("Listen: `venue_pickup_01` before, then after"))
display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / "venue_pickup_01_input.wav")))
display(Audio(filename=str(folder / "audio" / "venue_pickup_01_kip.wav")))"""))

cells.append(md("""## 6. Try it on any recording

Point this at any file from any device (an iPhone Voice Memo `.m4a` works): it prints the flagged moments and
writes `<name>.clean.wav` next to it. Same as `uv run python -m kipml.infer <file>` from the `ml/` folder."""))

cells.append(code("""from kipml.audio import load_any
from kipml.infer import segments

checkpoint = ML / "checkpoints" / ("handling-gpu.pt" if (ML / "checkpoints" / "handling-gpu.pt").exists() else "handling-poc.pt")
model = load_model(checkpoint)
print(f"{checkpoint.name}: {count_params(model):,} parameters")

recording = AUDIO / "ours" / "venue_pickup_02.wav"      # <- change me (this take was used in training)
x = load_any(recording)
clean, prob = enhance(model, x)
for s, e in segments(prob, 0.5, min_s=0.03):
    print(f"handling {s:6.2f} to {e:6.2f} s")
display(Audio(x, rate=RATE)); display(Audio(clean, rate=RATE))"""))

cells.append(md("""## Limits, honestly

- **Small, single-venue data**: about 3 minutes of real handling noise from one phone in one noisy hall, plus
  synthetic placeholders and ESC-50 backgrounds. Expect it to be best on that phone and that kind of room.
- **Detection is the strong part.** On the held-out drop take it flags the five drops and almost nothing else.
  Suppression on raw takes is modest; flagging the frame is what Kip needs (a flagged spike is never linked to a
  wake-up), and cleaner removal needs more and more varied recordings.
- **Quiet handling is not labelled**: sleeve rubbing that is not louder than the venue counts as room, by design.
- **Licences**: ESC-50 is CC BY-NC 3.0, fine for this prototype only. Our recordings were speech-checked before
  committing; recordings with other people's conversation never leave our machines."""))

nb.cells = cells
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {"name": "python3", "display_name": "Python 3 (ml/.venv)", "language": "python"}
nbf.write(nb, "notebooks/handling_poc.ipynb")
print("written", len(cells), "cells")

These results are from the Mac-trained model (v1), always on audio it never trained on.

**Training**
![training](</Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne/.context/charts/training.png>)

**Against a classic noise gate:** the model removes 8.5 dB where there's handling noise and leaves the room untouched (0.04 dB). The gate does the reverse: 1.2 dB on the handling noise and 5.5 dB taken out of the room.
![suppression](</Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne/.context/charts/suppression.png>)

**Your real held-out drop take:** it flags exactly the 5 drops (precision 0.85, recall 0.98) and leaves everything else alone.
![real take](</Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne/.context/charts/real_venue_pickup_01.png>)

**The honest part:** detection is the strong half. Suppression on raw takes is modest, about 3 dB off the drops. For Kip, flagging is what matters, because a flagged spike is never linked to a wake-up.

| On audio it never trained on | Mac model | **RTX 3090 model (shipped)** | Noise gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality gain (SI-SDR) | +2.6 dB | **+11.9 dB** | −3.9 dB |

I'm sketching out the rest of the doc: a short section on the results with a brief table and limits, then how the model plugs into Kip's server path. For the figures I want three new focused ones rather than reusing the big report pages: the input spectrogram with the drops visible, the learned mask over the same take, and either a reused suppression chart or a simple bar comparison against the gate.

I'm settling on reusing the existing suppression chart by linking to it, and generating two new figures for the input spectrogram and the learned mask. I'm thinking about a small reproducible script for those figures, with a sequential color ramp and plain labels.

I'm working out the theory section now: the STFT setup at 16 kHz with a 512-point FFT and 10 ms hop, which gives 257 frequency bins and 100 frames a second, and why the log compression matters for the 30 to 40 dB gap between drops and quiet room. I'm moving on to how the mask gets applied to the complex spectrogram.

I'm working through the architecture now: three strided convolutions that halve the frequency axis each time, a per-frame projection, and a bidirectional GRU so each frame can draw on the whole clip. The model ends in two heads, a sigmoid mask over the 257 bins and a single handling logit, and comes to roughly 419k parameters.

I'm checking how long inference takes on CPU for a 10-second clip, since the doc should state that number. The loss mixes a compressed magnitude L1 term with a 0.3-weighted BCE term on the handling label. Frame labels come from a rule based on the take's floor and the venue's 90th-percentile level, and the training mixtures are generated on the fly at varied SNRs and gains.

I'm going through the evaluation part now: the SI-SDR formula, how much energy gets removed per frame, and precision and recall. The spectral gate baseline estimates a steady noise floor per bin and subtracts it, so it clears the room tone but leaves the brief bursts behind. That makes it the wrong tool for handling noise. The results table and the limitations come last.

I'm checking the CPU inference time for a 10-second clip so the doc has a real number, and I'll write the figure script next. Then I'll write MODEL.md, link it from the README, and ship the PR.

"""Figures for ml/MODEL.md, from a real held-out take and the shipped model.

    cd ml && uv run python scripts/make_doc_figures.py
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ML = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ML))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch

from kipml import report as r                       # chart style and validated colours
from kipml.audio import AUDIO, HOP, RATE, frame_db, read_wav
from kipml.data import Clip, handling_labels, load_sources
from kipml.evaluate import load_model
from kipml.infer import segments
from kipml.model import features, stft

OUT = ML / "docs" / "img"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
TAKE = AUDIO / "ours" / "venue_pickup_01.wav"       # held out: never trained on

x = read_wav(TAKE)
model = load_model(ML / "checkpoints" / "handling-gpu.pt")
spec = stft(torch.from_numpy(x)[None])
with torch.no_grad():
    mask, logit = model(features(spec.abs()))
removed = 1.0 - mask[0].numpy().T                   # [freq, time]: 1 = fully removed
prob = torch.sigmoid(logit)[0].numpy()
venue = load_sources()["handling"]["test"]["ours"][0].venue_floor_db
labels = handling_labels(x, Clip(TAKE.name, x, float(np.percentile(frame_db(x), 10)), venue, True))
dur = len(x) / RATE

# 1. What the model sees
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 5), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True, gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1, 1.6]})
r._envelope(axes[0], x, r.INPUT)
axes[0].set_yticks([]); axes[0].set_title("Waveform: a phone set down five times in a noisy room")
r._spectrogram(axes[1], x, "Log-magnitude spectrogram (the model's input): each drop is a short, full-height stripe", r._spec_db(x).max())
axes[1].set_xlabel("seconds")
fig.savefig(OUT / "input.png", dpi=110); plt.close(fig)

# 2. What the model learned to remove
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 5), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True, gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1.6, 1]})
im = axes[0].imshow(removed, origin="lower", aspect="auto", cmap=r.SEQ, vmin=0, vmax=1, extent=[0, dur, 0, RATE / 2000])
axes[0].set_title("Mask: share of each time-frequency cell removed (dark = removed)"); axes[0].set_ylabel("kHz"); axes[0].grid(False)
cb = fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes[0], fraction=0.03, pad=0.01); cb.set_ticks([0, 0.5, 1]); cb.outline.set_visible(False)
for s, e in segments(labels.astype(float), 0.5, min_s=0.0, gap_s=0.0):
    axes[1].axvspan(s, e, color=r.GRID, linewidth=0)
axes[1].plot(np.arange(len(prob)) * HOP / RATE, prob, color=r.MODEL, linewidth=1.6)
axes[1].axhline(0.5, color=r.INK2, linewidth=0.8, linestyle=(0, (3, 3)))
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 1.02); axes[1].set_xlabel("seconds")
axes[1].set_title("Handling probability per 10 ms (grey: where the label says handling)")
fig.savefig(OUT / "mask.png", dpi=110); plt.close(fig)
print("wrote", OUT / "input.png", "and", OUT / "mask.png")

Both figures came out right: the input plot shows the drops as vertical stripes, and the mask removes exactly those five drops and nothing else. The colorbar's 0, 0.5, 1 scale works fine. Next I'll write a short, plain ml/MODEL.md with a Mermaid diagram, referencing docs/img/input.png and the other charts.

Next I'm drafting the doc's opening section on the handling problem: phone noise from fabric rubbing or knocks that could be mistaken for room noise in the wake-up attribution, which the filter is meant to find and remove. Then I'm setting out the input as an STFT spectrogram with a table of its window, hop, bins and log feature.

Now I'm describing what the handling noise looks like in the spectrogram: short bursts spread across all frequencies at once, unlike speech or traffic, which have structure across frequency and change more slowly. Next I'm laying out the network: three conv layers, a bidirectional GRU, and two output heads, one producing the mask and one the per-frame logit, with the GRU reading the whole clip in both directions so each frame gets context from before and after it.

Now I'm documenting the output side: the mask scales each spectrogram cell by a value between 0 and 1 and is applied with the input's phase, so it can only remove energy, never add sound. I'm also starting on the frame probability, which is turned into a detection with a 0.5 threshold.

Next I'm finishing the training data section: examples are mixed on the fly from a night background slice, with a 0.75 chance of adding a handling-noise slice scaled to between -5 and +20 dB against the background, and a random overall level between -30 and -3.

Now I'm finishing the training section: the splits are made by source recording, so the test sounds never appear in training. # How the handling filter works ## The problem A phone recording at night picks up its own handling: fabric rubbing over the microphone, the phone knocked or set down. To Kip these look like noise spikes. If they reached the wake-up attribution, Kip would blame the room for noise the phone made itself. The filter finds those moments, removes them, and leaves everything else alone. ## Input: a spectrogram The model never sees raw samples. It sees a short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of 16 kHz mono audio: | Setting | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | Window | 25 ms Hann (400 samples), zero-padded to 512 | long enough to resolve frequency, short enough for a knock | | Hop | 10 ms (160 samples) | one frame every 10 ms | | Bins | 257, from 0 to 8 kHz, 31.25 Hz apart | | | Feature | `log(1 + 10 * abs(X))` | a quiet room and a loud knock differ by 30 to 40 dB; the log keeps both visible | Handling noise has a clear shape in this picture: short, and spread across every frequency at once. Speech, traffic and snoring have structure in frequency and change more slowly. ![What the model sees](docs/img/input.png) ## The network ```mermaid flowchart LR A["log-magnitude
T x 257"] --> B["3 conv layers, 32 channels
257 to 129 to 65 to 33 bins"] B --> C["per frame: linear
1056 to 128"] C --> D["bidirectional GRU
128 each way"] D --> E["mask head
T x 257, sigmoid"] D --> F["frame head
T x 1, logit"] ``` - **Convolutions** look at small time-frequency patches (3 x 5, then 3 x 3) and halve the frequency resolution each time. They pick up local shapes, such as a vertical stripe. - **The GRU** reads the clip forwards and backwards, so each frame is judged against what the room sounds like before and after it. A knock is easier to spot when you know the background. - **Two heads**: a mask with one value per time-frequency cell, and one handling logit per frame. - 418,754 parameters, 1.6 MB as ONNX. A 10-second clip takes about 21 ms on one CPU thread in ONNX Runtime (90 ms in PyTorch, including the STFT). ## Two outputs **Mask, for suppression.** Each cell of the input spectrogram X is multiplied by a value M between 0 and 1, and the inverse STFT turns the result back into audio, reusing the input's phase: `S_hat = M * X`. A mask can only remove energy, never add sound, which is the safe way for a filter to fail. **Frame probability, for detection.** `sigmoid(logit) > 0.5` marks a 10 ms frame as handling noise. This is the part Kip relies on: a spike flagged as handling gets the label `handling` and is never linked to a wake-up. ![What the model removes](docs/img/mask.png) On this held-out take the mask removes five narrow columns, one per drop, and leaves the room between them untouched. ## Training data There are only about 3 minutes of real handling noise, so training examples are mixed on the fly: 1. a 4-second slice of a night background: ESC-50 clips, plus venue room tone on our own machines; 2. with probability 0.75, a slice of handling noise (our iPhone takes, or synthetic placeholders), scaled to between -5 and +20 dB against the background; 3. a random overall level between -30 and -3 dBFS. Every example is new, so the model cannot memorise the mixtures, only the sounds. Splits are by source recording, so no test sound is ever heard in training. **Labels.** A 10 ms frame counts as handling noise when the take is louder there than its own quiet floor by 8 dB, and louder than the venue: the 90th percentile of the venue room tone, plus 3 dB. Our takes were recorded in a loud hall; without the second condition, the crowd behind them would be labelled as handling. **Target.** The background plus the quiet parts of the take. The model learns to remove the bursts, not the room around them. ## Loss `L = mean(abs((M * abs(X))^0.3 - abs(S)^0.3)) + 0.3 * BCE(logit, label)` - The first term compares the cleaned spectrogram with the target. The 0.3 power compresses magnitudes roughly the way hearing does, so quiet detail still counts next to a loud knock. - The second term trains the frame detector. AdamW, learning rate 0.002 with cosine decay, batch 32, 15,000 steps, gradients clipped at 5: 15 minutes on an RTX 3090. ![Training curves](reports/handling-gpu/training.png) ## How it is measured Every number below is on mixtures and recordings the model never trained on. - **SI-SDR improvement**: the scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio of the output against the target, minus the same for the input. With `a = / |s|^2`, `SI-SDR = 10 * log10(|a*s|^2 / |a*s - s_hat|^2)`. Higher is better, and overall volume does not matter. - **Energy removed** per frame, split into frames that are handling noise and frames that are not. The ideal is a lot, then nothing. - **Precision and recall** of the frame detector against the labels. **Baseline: spectral gating.** The standard noise-reduction method estimates each frequency's steady level (here the 20th percentile over time) and subtracts it. That assumes stationary noise. Handling noise is the opposite, short bursts far above any steady level, so a gate mostly leaves it and takes its cut from the room instead. ![Model against a spectral gate](reports/handling-gpu/suppression.png) ## Results | Held-out | Model | Spectral gate | |---|---|---| | SI-SDR improvement, median of 150 mixtures | +11.9 dB | -3.9 dB | | Energy removed on handling frames | 17.9 dB | 1.2 dB | | Energy removed on room-only frames | 0.15 dB | 5.5 dB | | Frame detection, precision / recall | 0.90 / 0.92 | n/a | | Real drop take, precision / recall | 0.96 / 1.00 | n/a | | Real drop take, energy removed on the drops / elsewhere | 27.8 / 0.2 dB | n/a | ## Limits - Trained on one iPhone in one loud hall. Expect it to work best on that kind of recording. - Strongest on knocks and drops. Slow rustling is caught less often and removed less: on the held-out walking-pocket take, recall 0.73 and 12.5 dB removed. - Rustling quieter than the room is not labelled as handling, by design: it cannot cause a spike. - ESC-50 is CC BY-NC 3.0, so this model is for the prototype only. ## Where it runs The plan (#90, #91): the API computes the STFT, runs `models/handling-poc.onnx`, applies the mask and reads the frame probabilities (the contract is in `models/README.md`). Spikes whose frames are mostly handling are labelled `handling` and skip Gemini. To try it on any recording: `uv run python -m kipml.infer `. Regenerate the two figures above with `uv run python scripts/make_doc_figures.py`.
